section_summary: Pages 303–327 contain the end of one copy and three further copies of an article standardizing terminology for the Japan Communist Party’s structure, offices, publications and meetings. A Tokyo despatch and its enclosed conversation memorandum assess divisions within the Social Democratic Party, its labor and farmer support, and possible future leaders. The section ends with a heavily damaged airgram concerning demonstrations and police action in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Concluding definitions of Communist Party headquarters offices, publications and meetings.
subfiles.summary: The article names central bureaus and their duties, describes party directives and publications, and sets out the powers and schedules of national, regional, prefectural and district meetings. It urges consistent terminology in intelligence reporting.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology
subfiles.about: A reference guide to English and romanized Japanese terms for Communist Party organization.
subfiles.summary: The article defines party echelons from the Central Committee to cells, distinguishes fractions from factions, and explains position titles and headquarters bureaus. It describes official documents, publications and meetings at each organizational level. Its stated purpose is to make intelligence reporting more consistent; it cites a February 1949 terminology guide as a source.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology
subfiles.about: Another copy of the guide to Japan Communist Party organizational terminology.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the definitions of party committees, cells, fractions, officers, bureaus, publications and meetings. It includes a chart of command echelons and warns against misleading translations of party terms.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology
subfiles.about: A further copy of the guide to Communist Party structure and terminology.
subfiles.summary: The article again supplies standard names for the party’s hierarchy, positions and central offices, with explanations of its publications and conferences. It distinguishes infiltration fractions from political factions and recommends uniform wording for intelligence reports.

subfiles.title: Future of the Social Democratic Party, despatch no. 332
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits an interview with Yonekubo Mitsusuke and assesses the Socialist Party’s factions and prospects.
subfiles.summary: Huston reports Yonekubo’s expectation of an eventual left–right split and his intention to join the left. The despatch weighs possible younger leaders, losses of established figures and the growing influence of organized labor, especially the Democratization League.

subfiles.title: Future of the Social Democratic Party
subfiles.about: Records Yonekubo Mitsusuke’s views on Socialist Party leadership, labor and farmer support, and elections.
subfiles.summary: Yonekubo predicts a party split within a year or two, discusses rival secretary general candidates and identifies promising younger politicians. He assesses the Democratization League, Sōdōmei and farmers’ unions, explains the effects of losing older leaders, and expects the party to rebuild through local organization and stronger ties to laborers and farmers.

subfiles.title: Airgram concerning Tokyo demonstrations
subfiles.about: Reports on demonstrations, proposed assembly rules and police action in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The damaged text refers to disorderly demonstrations, proposed advance notice for assemblies, police dispersal, arrests and injuries.
